title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The verso is handwritten on the back of a typed SGA 7 Exposé IX page about 'extensions panachées' of Barsotti–Tate groups; the typescript is unrelated to the manuscript. The handwritten text belongs to the notes for the 1976 IHÉS talk on the divided-power de Rham complex. The page is a short passage that sets up coefficients.

The passage reads as follows. For an object X (a space, simplicial set or scheme-like object in the talk), there is an integral 'chain' version C_*^{DR,pd}(X) := C_*^{DR,pd}(X; Z) of a divided-power (pd) de Rham complex. The version over an arbitrary base ring k is obtained by base change, C_*^{DR,pd}(X,k) ≃ C_*^{DR,pd}(X) ⊗_Z k. The 'cochain' (cohomological) version is defined by duality, C^*_{DR,pd}(X,k) ≃ Hom(C_*^{DR,pd}(X,k), k), equivalently Hom_Z(C_*^{DR,pd}(X), k).

More generally, for any abelian group M, and functorially in M, he sets
- C_*^{DR,pd}(X,M) := C_*^{DR,pd}(X) ⊗_Z M
- C^*_{DR,pd}(X,M) := Hom(C_*^{DR,pd}(X), M)

He then remarks that the structures carried by C_*^{DR,pd}(X) (presumably coalgebra / divided-power-dual structures) induce 'a host of multiplicative structures' on these functors of M.

This is the standard universal-coefficient formalism: build one integral object, get all coefficients by ⊗ and Hom. Its purpose in the project is to produce an integral, pd-based model whose specializations give cohomology with arbitrary coefficients together with products. One plausible reading is a divided-power analogue of Sullivan's polynomial forms over Z, though this page alone does not say so.
errors: The formula Hom(C_*^{DR,pd}(X,k)) omits the target. It should read Hom_k(C_*(X,k), k), which is ≅ Hom_Z(C_*(X), k).

Defining cochains with M-coefficients as an underived Hom, and identifying C(X,k) with C(X) ⊗ k, gives the right (co)homology only if C_*^{DR,pd}(X) is degreewise free or flat (or if one passes to derived ⊗/RHom). This is not stated on the page, though it presumably holds for the complexes in question.
The phrase 'a host of multiplicative structures' is a promissory remark; none are specified here.

ideas.what: Define an integral pd de Rham chain complex once, and obtain arbitrary coefficients by C ⊗_Z M (chains) and Hom(C, M) (cochains), functorially in M.
ideas.modern_name: Universal coefficients / extension of scalars for a free integral chain model
ideas.where_published: Analogous formalism appears in SGA 4/SGA 5 style coefficient discussions; this specific pd de Rham setting is unpublished as far as known.

ideas.what: Multiplicative structures on the coefficient functors in M, induced from structure on the integral chain object (e.g. a coalgebra structure inducing cup products).
ideas.modern_name: Cup/cap products from a (pd-)coalgebra or E_∞ structure on integral chains
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Alexander–Whitney/cup products); the integral pd-forms context relates to H. Cartan's 1976 'Théories cohomologiques' and later integral rational-homotopy work

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains only routine definitions extending an integral pd de Rham chain complex to arbitrary coefficients, plus an unspecified remark about multiplicative structures. Any interest lies in the broader 1976 project, not in this page.
transcription_corrections: The garbled line 'et [?] [?] de [?] =' is a handwritten connective introducing the dual (cochain) version; plausibly 'et de même dualement' or similar. It is illegible in detail.
In 'Hom(C_·^{DR,pd}(X,k))' the target is missing in the transcription. The image appears to read 'Hom(C_·^{DR,pd}(X), k)' or 'Hom(C_·^{DR,pd}(X,k), k)'.
In the first displayed formula the handwriting has a lower-dot subscript on the C, as on the other chain complexes, rather than C_* with an asterisk on the right-hand side.
The underlying typed text, visible through the paper, is SGA 7 Exp. IX material and should not be mixed into the handwritten transcription.
